fields.acceptance: make -n test shows go test with -skip of the budget tests, no -run of them and no 'Timing budgets' phase; make -n test-budgets shows them run -count=1 -p 1 over ./internal/api ./internal/index ./internal/slice; BUDGET_TESTS is ^(TestReadBudget|TestReadBudgetApply|TestBudget|TestCatchUpBudget|TestDriverPollIsCheap)$ and each name matches a test go test -list finds in those packages (@{01M7ESH0D6NJ2X7HZSR1XW9G58}); go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run '^(TestMakeTestTimeout|TestMakeTestShardTargets|TestMakeUpdateDryRun)$' passes with its expected commands updated; .github/workflows/ci.yml's budgets job still runs make test-budgets; make help shows make check without 'everything CI runs' and naming make test-budgets as the CI run it leaves out, and AGENTS.md's Commands block line for make check says the same (no 'everything CI runs' left in either: grep -n 'everything CI runs' Makefile AGENTS.md prints nothing); failure case: TestMakeTestTimeout or TestMakeTestShardTargets fails when make test's recipe runs a budget test. Speedup measure (orchestrator, quiet VM): a warm /usr/bin/time -f '%e s' make test, against 254 s, expected about 70 s since the budget phase took 188 s, with no 'Timing budgets' phase in its output. Touches Makefile (test's and check's help text and check's comment), cmd/rhiza/makeupdate_test.go, AGENTS.md (the '(and the timing budgets)' lock sentence, make test's description and the Commands block's 'make check # everything CI runs' line). Must not drop a budget test from test-budgets or change a budget limit.
fields.statement: make test and make check no longer run the timing budgets: the budget phase leaves make test's recipe, the budgets run only in the opt-in make test-budgets (alone, -count=1 -p 1, printing the read-budget timings), which CI's budgets job runs on every pull request, and AGENTS.md and the Makefile's comments say so.
